value: apposition compound eye (the authors' wording is 'It seems')
method: scanning electron microscopy of the eye surface and of a cross section of one eye (no TEM or histology of the eye)
conditions: One dead adult male (n = 1) from a 250 W light trap at Montagne de Kaw, Camp Patawa, French Guiana, 12 January 2019, decapitated under CO2 anaesthesia and examined within 10 days; eye dehydrated, critical-point dried and gold-coated. The Results sentence says it looks as if a clear zone between the dioptric apparatus and the photoreceptive structures was not developed, so the eye resembled an apposition eye; the eye holds hundreds of ommatidia, regular facets centrally and irregular ones at the periphery, and the number of retinula and pigment cells per ommatidium is undetermined. The authors add that the beetle flies at night, that its apposition ommatidium also suggests diurnal activity ('We can neither confirm nor deny this based on available literature') and that 'one individual is not sufficient for a deep ground-breaking study'. Females not examined.
